A '''urethral obstruction''' is a life-threatening emergency in male cats.
== Presentation == * Straining to urinate * Vocalising, often in the litter box * A hard, distended bladder on palpation
== Immediate actions == # Place an IV catheter and start fluids. # Draw a blood gas & biochemistry panel — hyperkalaemia kills first. # Decompress the bladder by cystocentesis if the patient is unstable.
> '''Warning:''' do not attempt catheterisation before the patient has been stabilised.
See also [[Hyperkalaemia management]].

Potassium above 7 mmol/L requires immediate treatment.
{| class="wikitable" ! ECG finding !! Action |- | Peak… T waves || Calcium gluconate 10%, 0.5 mL/kg slow IV |- | Absent P waves || Insulin 0.1 U/kg with dextrose |}
